title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 81
paragraphs: Then having gathered the things together, and set apart a tithe for the god at Delphi (with which was dedicated the golden tripod that rests upon the three-headed bronze serpent and stands close by the altar), and also for the god at Olympia (with which they dedicated a bronze statue of Zeus ten cubits high), and finally for the god at the Isthmus (with which was made a bronze statue of Poseidon seven cubits high) — having set apart these things, they divided the rest, and each took what they were due, including the concubines of the Persians and the gold, silver, and other things, and also the beasts of burden. How much was set apart and given to those who had proved the best men at Plataea is not reported by anyone, though for my part I suppose gifts were made to them too. To Pausanias, however, ten of each thing were set apart and given — women, horses, talents, camels, and so on for the other things.
